title: Y Turns Into I
kidRule: When a word ends in a consonant and then Y, you usually change the Y to I before adding an ending: hurry becomes hurried and country becomes countries. Keep the Y if a vowel comes before it (plays) or if the ending is ING (hurrying).
hint: Think of the small word hiding in here. Its last letter changes when an ending joins on. What does it change to?
reminder: Change the Y to I before you add the ending.

check.question: Why is there an I in HURRIED when HURRY ends with Y?
check.correctAnswer: When a word ends in a consonant and Y, the Y changes to I before the ending!
distractors: Because Y is never allowed in the middle of any word
Because I and Y take turns, and it was I's turn

words.why: HURRY changes its Y to I before E-D is added.
words.def: Moved or did something very fast.
words.sent: We hurried to the bus stop in the rain.
words.story: A cheetah can speed up from standing still to as fast as a car on the highway in about three seconds!
words.card: '*Hurr*ay!' yelled the snail as it *hurried* past a sleeping turtle!

words.why: COUNTRY changes its Y to I before E-S is added.
words.def: Lands with their own people, flags, and leaders, like Japan, Kenya, and Brazil.
words.sent: Our class learned about three countries in Africa.
words.story: There are almost 200 countries in the world, and the smallest one, Vatican City, is smaller than many city parks!
words.card: Can you *count* all the *countries* on a spinning globe before you get dizzy?

words.why: EASY changes its Y to I before E-R is added.
words.sent: Riding a bike gets easier every time you try.
words.story: The wheel was invented more than 5,000 years ago, and it made moving heavy things much easier!
words.card: Swimming is *easier* when you are *as* slippery *as* a seal!

words.why: STORY changes its Y to I before E-S is added.
words.def: Tales about people and things that happen, real or made up.
words.sent: Grandpa tells the best bedtime stories.
words.story: Before there were books, people passed stories along by telling them out loud and remembering them!
words.card: I told *stories* *to* my toes until they fell asleep!

words.why: CARRY changes its Y to I before E-D is added.
words.def: Held something and took it from one place to another.
words.sent: Dad carried the sleepy puppy upstairs.
words.story: Long ago, mail in the American West was carried by riders on fast horses called the Pony Express!
words.card: The snail *carried* a toy *car* on its shell!

words.why: HAPPY changes its Y to I before N-E-S-S is added.
words.def: The feeling of being glad and cheerful.
words.sent: Her face was full of happiness when she saw the cake.
words.story: The whole world celebrates the International Day of Happiness every year on March 20!
words.card: *Happiness* is a *pin*k pig in a puddle!

words.why: FUNNY changes its Y to I before E-S-T is added.
words.def: Making people laugh more than anything else.
words.sent: That was the funniest joke I ever heard.
words.story: People are not the only ones who laugh: chimpanzees and gorillas laugh when they are tickled!
words.card: The *funniest* part of the *fun* fair was the burping clown fish!

words.why: MEMORY changes its Y to I before E-S is added.
words.sent: Grandpa shared happy memories of his childhood farm.
words.story: Smells are especially good at bringing back old memories, because the smelling part of the brain is closely linked to the remembering part!
words.card: I wrote a *memo* so my *memories* of the pie contest would never fade!

words.why: BEAUTY changes its Y to I before F-U-L is added.
words.def: Very lovely to look at or listen to.
words.sent: We watched a beautiful sunset over the sea.
words.story: Seen up close, snowflakes are beautiful ice crystals with six sides or six arms!
words.card: *If* a slug wears a bow tie, is it *beautiful*?

words.why: LONELY changes its Y to I before N-E-S-S is added.
words.def: The sad feeling of being all by yourself and wishing for company.
words.sent: A phone call from a friend chased away her loneliness.
words.story: Guinea pigs like company so much that in Switzerland the rules say you should not keep just one all by itself!
words.card: Just *one* hug from a penguin can melt away *loneliness*!
